newsitem.title: MEXICO: Peso closes up as foreigners enter Mexico markets.
newsitem.headline: Peso closes up as foreigners enter Mexico markets.

text.p: The peso extended early strength at the close on Tuesday as dealers decided to dump dollars and invest in the Mexican stock and money markets, traders said.
"We felt there was a real capital inflow after midsession...this also led locals to dump dollars," a trader said.
"Foreigners seem to have been waiting , in vain, to enter the market, waiting for a better rate (in pesos)," he added.
The 48-hour and 24-hour peso closed 1.85 and 1.9 centavos stronger respectively, to 7.5185/7.5225 and 7.5140/7.5190 per dollar.
Traders said that the move by foreigners into the Mexican money and stock markets was fueled by yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds falling again.
"Long-bond yields are below 6.90 percent, and that tends to make investors in the U.S. bond market look elsewhere," a trader said.
The same-day peso earlier closed 2.3 centavos higher at 7.5220/7.5250 per dollar.
Traders said they expected Wednesday's session to be influenced by Tuesday's Cetes auction results.
A survey conducted by Reuters among 10 money market operators showed they expected the bellwether 28-day Cetes rate to fall by an average of 23 basis points.
